title: Generative artificial intelligence: a systematic review and applications
extended_summary:
This paper presents a systematic review of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) research, focusing on recent advancements, model variants, and application areas. The authors aim to synthesize the state of the art across major generative paradigms, including GANs, transformers, variational autoencoders, and diffusion models, and to discuss how these methods have evolved over time. The review also emphasizes responsible AI considerations, including ethical issues and sustainability concerns.

The paper is not an intervention study with human participants. Instead, it surveys peer-reviewed literature from 2012–2023, primarily sourced through Google Scholar, and organizes the findings by application domain. These domains include image translation, video synthesis and generation, natural language processing, and several specialized uses such as synthetic data generation and molecule generation. Within each domain, the paper summarizes representative methods, benchmark datasets, and evaluation metrics used in prior work.

The review concludes that GenAI has achieved major progress in language generation, image translation, and other interdisciplinary applications, with transformers and large language models driving particularly strong advances in text-related tasks. It also highlights that unpaired image translation, video generation, and multilingual NLP are active areas of development, but that challenges remain around training stability, performance evaluation, and ethical deployment. Because the paper is a broad technical review rather than a study of K-12 learners or classroom implementation, it does not report participant populations, user roles, or educational intervention outcomes.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s GPT-based large language model chatbot/system for generating and understanding text.
identified_tools.use_case: Cited as one of the models evaluated in the paper’s discussion of summarization on QMSUM and as a generative AI system in educational contexts; also mentioned in the paper’s broader review of NLP applications.

findings.finding_summary: On QMSUM, ChatGPT achieved the best ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-2 scores among the compared summarization systems, but not the best ROUGE-L. The paper reports ROUGE-1 = 36.83, ROUGE-2 = 12.78, and ROUGE-L = 24.23 for ChatGPT on QMSUM, compared with HMNet’s higher ROUGE-L of 31.27.
findings.measure: Text summarization quality on QMSUM using ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review paper, not a primary educational intervention study. The reported evidence is secondary synthesis and includes benchmark comparisons rather than a controlled study design.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports performance metrics from summarization benchmarks, but no effect sizes or K-12 learning outcomes are provided. The impact on education is indirect and not specific to subgroup or instructional settings.
